newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures end off peaks on origin sales.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures end off peaks on origin sales.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures were broadly firmer by the close on Tuesday but most positions were below their ceiling on scale-up producer selling, traders said.

Prices dipped at the start on commission house selling. But a technical rally in New York on an unexpected drop in U.S. certified stocks boosted gains in London, triggering a few buy-stops on the way up.
Most active March surged to a high of $1,322 a tonne before ending $21 up on the day at $1,310 on selling by origins.
"Producers had been holding off a little bit but I think today is a good opportunity to sell," said one.
"There's a lot of robusta around and there's no real reason why it should go up much more with the adequate stocks there are and the adequate shipments being made at the moment," he added.

London's advance however stopped short of re-testing last week's high of $1,335. Further barriers are placed at $1,355 and $1,400. New York arabica futures basis March flew to test a new high of 122.25 cents a lb boosted by commission house and fund buying amid the draw in the certifieds. The stocks stored in U.S. warehouses fell by 9,070 60-kg bags in the week to January 10 to 23,388 bags, the Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange said after Monday's close. No coffee was pending grading or recerfitication.

Players are now awaiting for the closely-watched Green Coffee Association monthly stocks figures. The data due after New York's close on Wednesday are expected to provide a broader picture on the supply situation in the United States.
London's LIFFE December certified stocks are also due by lunchtime on Wednesday. Key African producers are in Vietnam to lobby Indonesia and Vietnam to rein in exports to boost soft robusta prices.
But traders were skeptical that both the top Asian growers would back African efforts to bolster prices by cutting exports.

The market's volume reached 5,089 lots while the March/March arbitrage between New York and London widened to 62 cents on Tuesday from just below 60 cents last week. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
